findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: There were no paper towels at the handwashing sink at the start of the inspection. CORRECTED- The employee replaced the paper towels. findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: There are no Chlorine test strips available to test the concentration of the Chlorine sanitizer in the dish machine. A follow up is scheduled for 2/5/2026 to ensure that Chlorine test strips have been obtained. There should always be test strips for every type of sanitizer that is being used in a facility to ensure that food-contact surfaces are being sanitized at a label-recommended concentration.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: The faucet of the triple sink in the kitchen is observed to have a dripping leak coming from it. Ensure that this leak is repaired. All plumbing systems should be maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment:
REPEAT- There is not a temperature measuring device observed in the following coolers: 

1. The Grab and Go Drink Cooler.
2. The Grab and Go Cooler containing Uncrustables and other food items. 
3. The yogurt cooler in the buffet area. 

Ensure that every cold and hot holding unit has a temperature measuring device located in either the warmest part of a refrigerated unit or in the coolest part of a hot holding unit.
findings.citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment: The bulk dispensers of cereal and the clear display case containing breads, muffins, bagels, etc. are both observed to not have proper allergen labeling. The facility has placed the Notice to Consumer Allergen poster in both areas, but this is not sufficient. There needs to be either a placard, labels, a poster, or some other method that clearly indicates the allergens that are in each item for consumers to be able to easily view. Bulk food that is available for consumer self-dispensing needs to have allergen labeling posted for consumers.
findings.citation_text: 3-602.11(C) Food Labels. (C) Bulk FOOD that is available for CONSUMER self-dispensing shall be prominently labeled with the following information in plain view of the CONSUMER: (1) The manufacturer's or processor's label that was provided with the FOOD; or (2) A card, sign, or other method of notification that includes the information specified under Subparagraphs (B)(1), (2), (5) and (6) of this section.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The walk-in cooler fan cover is observed to have an accumulation of dust on it and needs to be cleaned. Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

(B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Observed no date mark on dairy-based half & half. Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment: 410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Present employee has been working in kitchen for three months and has not completed food handler training. Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  Reference 410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment: 750-140(b)  Observed breakfast being closed and foods being cooled improperly. See notes in General Comments: indicate the time on the cooling foods and cool uncovered in shallow pans. Pans of homestyle potatoes and sausage patties were being placed in a covered container in bulk. Halted process and discussed with staff. Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 140°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment: 750-530a The kitchen is compact and has little space for personal storage. See that clock, phone, and beverages are stored on one side of the counter and not on top of seasoning shakers and oatmeal. Moved during inspection - keep personal separate from facility foods/items.  Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750-690 Observed bath towels being placed on working island to aide in ease of clean-up. Cease use of cloths. Prepare foods on cleanable, non-porous materials. Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment: 750-820d The quat sanitizing solution was empty. A third sink was filled as was buckets with this solution. Operator was unaware of the lack of chemical, manager was aware. Discussed insuring that staff was aware of the lack of proper solution. Quat was restocked to 200 ppm during inspection: bucket and sink refilled.  Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4).

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: 750-810b There was not a sani-bucket available in the kitchen. The lobby quat bucket is observed at 0 ppm Quat (see #20). Corrected during the inspection. Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750-690 Several non-food items are observed in various conditions: 1) the laminate is peeling from some of the shelves within the service area (seal); 2) pink cloths are being used within the utensil drawers (discussed purpose of this), remove and simply add drawers to routine cleaning; and 3) cardboard between single-service bronze containers.   Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: 750-1220 Floors throughout are observed clean. The floor drain beneath the mop sink has minimal mold growth. Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: 750-151(a) Bulk milk is observed without a proper day dot. During the week, milk may last within dispenser for two or three days. Label milk with date of opening and use or discard within seven days. Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: 750-1220 Floors throughout are observed clean. The floor mat in-front of the triple sink is observed coated with crumbs and grease from multiple days' use. Clean the floor mat.  Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: 750-250 The waffle batter has no time as control policy and is observed in storage unit without a cold pack at 64F.   Created a Time As Control policy during the inspection. Facility is not allowed to keep the product unless a temperature log is maintained and food can be held at 41F or below. With only one ice pack at the base of the unit, the majority of the food is likely NOT going to be properly temperature held. All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited

Research available enzymatic cleaners to see if one of them will suit your needs - cleaning floor drains and discharge lines beneath equipment can be problematic. Effective measures to minimize the presence of rodents and insects shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...

Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similar equipment shall be maintained and stored in a way that does not contaminate food.

findings.title: Clean and soiled linen segregated and properly stored.

Properly store soiled linens.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory

CORRECTED> Observed a container of cooling gravy to not be properly time marked with the time the food was removed from hot holding. Staff stated she had removed the gravy at ~9:06 AM. Time was indicated on a white board and cooling practices were discussed with staff. Violation immediately corrected.
750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
About three quarts of waffle batter found in glass door cooler at 54 degrees F (probe).  Staff state it was made at 5:30am and placed in waffle dispenser on breakfast bar.  It had been pulled off breakfast bar and placed into cooler at approximately 9:30.  Time as a Control policy had been discussed on a prior inspection - based on this policy, batter should be made, then used or discarded, in four hours.  Leftover batter that has been stored above 41 degrees F cannot be returned to cooler for use the next day.  CORRECTED - batter was immediately, voluntarily, discarded.  Time as a Control policy was located, incomplete.  Staff and inspector immediately completed policy form and a copy given for health dept file.
750-153(a) Food shall not be held more that 4 hours past the point it is removed from temperature control. Do not hold food in excess of four hours after removal from temperature control.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment:
[1]  Approximately 6 quarts of minestrone soup, cooked and served last night, was found in vertical cooler at 48-50 degrees F (probed multiple times).  CORRECTED - food was immediately, voluntarily discarded.
[2] About 3 lb of prepared macaroni and cheese, cooked and served last night, was found in vertical cooler at 49 degrees F (probed multiple times).  CORRECTED - food was immediately, voluntarily discarded.

Both containers of food items were prepared for supper last night, and removed from hot holding temperatures at approximately 7pm.  Found at ~9:45 this morning, more than 12 hours later, at temperatures above 41 degrees would indicate that foods were not properly cooled.  This history of the two containers was thoroughly discussed with kitchen staff and manager, as was proper cooling practices.
